ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, fold $\triangle ABC$ along the segment $DE$ so that point $B$ falls on point $F$; if $AC \parallel DE$, $\angle A = 70^\circ$, $AB = AC$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle CEF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: We fold triangle $ABC$ along the line segment $DE$, such that point $B$ falls on point $F$,\\
thus, triangle $BDE \cong FDE$,\\
hence, $\angle DEB = \angle DEF$,\\
since $\angle A=70^\circ$, and $AB=AC$,\\
thus, $\angle B = \angle C = \frac{1}{2} \times (180^\circ - 70^\circ) = 55^\circ$,\\
since $AC \parallel DE$,\\
hence, $\angle DEB = \angle C = 55^\circ = \angle DEF$,\\
thus, $\angle FEC = 180^\circ - \angle DEB - \angle DEF = \boxed{70^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, BC is the base, B is at the lower left, and C is at the lower right; D is located on the side where the left side AB is, E is located on the base BC, and the crease is line segment DE; after B is folded, it lands on point F on the right side AC. In the figure there are line segments from D to F and from E to F, as well as a curved arrow indicating the folding direction, and the dashed lines indicate the original BD and BE. The problem statement gives AC ∥ DE, ∠A = 70°, AB = AC. Reasoning: Because AB = AC, △ABC is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles are equal, that is, ∠B = ∠C. Also ∠A = 70°, so ∠B = ∠C = (180° - 70°) / 2 = 55°. Since AC ∥ DE, and EB is on the line BC, ∠DEB and ∠C are correspondingly equal, therefore ∠DEB = 55°. The folding is carried out along DE, B lands on F, reflection preserves angles, and DE is the angle bisector of ∠BEF, therefore ∠DEF = ∠DEB = 55°. Also EB and EC are opposite rays on the same straight line, so the straight angle from EB to EC is 180°, which contains ∠DEB, ∠DEF, and ∠FEC, therefore ∠CEF = 180° - 55° - 55° = 70°.
